[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Thomas Glascoe''' married [[Duffy-?|Margaret Duffy]], daughter of [[Duffy-?|Patrick Duffy]] and his wife Anne.

An undated handwritten pedigree of the Duffy family identifies Margaret as:

: “Margt, wife of Thomas Glascoe”

Margaret’s father, Patrick Duffy, was associated with Back Lane, Dublin. The pedigree states that Patrick made his will on 9 April 1774 and that it was proved in June 1775.

The pedigree also names Margaret’s siblings as John Duffy, Peter Duffy, Judith Duffy, Mary Duffy, and possibly Teresa Duffy. Judith married Cornelius Blewitt.

No children of Thomas and Margaret are shown on the pedigree. This does not prove that they had no children.

== Research Notes ==
=== Trinity family comparison ===

Select [[Glasco-144|Thomas Glasco]] as the Trinity student John’s probable working father at 63% subjective confidence. The original college entry names father Thomas, described as Artifex (craftsman), and says John was born in Dublin. The preferred existing account is the Dublin Thomas already tentatively identified with the watchmaker active in 1773–1783. The uncommon full name, same city, appropriate adult generation and actual craft occupation together make that account a better fit than name and age alone. A further family clue is the 1784 Dublin baptism of John, son of Thomas Glasco and Eliza Hynes: the 1779 watchmaker’s marriage names Miss Hynes. The directory independently supplies Thomas’s forename and the exact Ormond Quay address of the watchmaker; the bracketed Thomas in the marriage extraction is editorial, not another independent name statement.

Prefer the 1784 St Michan’s baptism and the 1800 Trinity student as one John at 72% subjective confidence. Both name John Glasco/Glascow, father Thomas and Dublin; the college age of 16 on 10 June 1800 puts a literal birth window at 11 June 1783–10 June 1784, compatible with a later 17 September 1784 baptism but not a recorded birthday. The Hynes marriage/baptism correspondence and the father’s craft description give the proposed family more specificity than a date-and-name match. The Catholic baptism and scholarship in 1803 leave a material religious-history gap: contemporary accounts describe exclusion of Catholics from scholarships. A baptismal affiliation need not remain unchanged throughout life, but no conversion or mixed-marriage history has been found or inferred. Another John or another Thomas remains possible.

Select the record-defined Eliza Hynes as John’s probable mother at 72%, conditional on the preferred baptism-to-student identity. The baptism transcript expressly names her as mother of its John; the college page names no mother. Her identification with the watchmaker’s 1779 Miss Hynes is a further probable comparison, not a recorded marriage for this named Eliza. No marriage to [[Glasco-144|Thomas Glasco]] is installed, and the Duffy, Catherine and Mary King households retain their own identities and grades.

The 63% father estimate assesses the whole link to the modern [[Glasco-144|Thomas]] account, including its unresolved watchmaker identification; it is lower than confidence that the printed student had a father named Thomas. [[Glasco-173|Thomas]]’s 1760 Sarah/Catherine household, [[Glasco-143|Thomas]] and an unrepresented namesake remain alternatives. [[Glasco-173|Thomas]] has no independently recorded trade in the reviewed baptism. The baptism is a Findmypast transcript, not an inspected original; North Anne Street is the church/parish description, not a proved family address. These subjective percentages are not measured frequencies or independent values to multiply. John’s later identity remains on HOLD: [[Glasgow-3946|John Glascow]], died at Thurles 1871 aged 87, and [[Glasgow-3751|John Glasgow]] of the 1820 Abbeville census remain compatible comparisons. No identity merge, live WikiTree edit, exact birth date, father replacement or new connection between existing profile components is claimed.

Inspect the 1784 original baptism for sponsors and address, obtain the specific 1871 Thurles death certificate for occupation and informant, and trace the 1805 graduate into clergy, professional or other records. A surviving compatible candidate prevents new WikiTree creation. Check the 1779 marriage original and further Dublin household records before treating Miss Hynes as named Eliza or transferring spouses between Thomas profiles.<ref>[https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FIE0004%2F364&parentid=IRE%2FIE0004%2F364%2F009 Burtchaell and Sadleir, Alumni Dublinenses (1924), printed p. 328, Findmypast image 364: John Glascow (Glasco) and Manasses Glascow; original printed page inspected 21 October 2026]. === Preferred Dublin father — 18 October 2026 ===

Philip [[Glasco-146]] replaces Thomas [[Glasco-173]] as the selected probable father, 67%. The 1773 Dublin groom/watchmaker identity is preferred, not proved.

Select Philip [[Glasco-146]], the provisional elder Dublin watchmaker account, as the probable working father of Thomas [[Glasco-144]] at 67% subjective confidence. The maintained reading of the 1773 advertisement explicitly says that Thomas served his apprenticeship to his father Philip Glasco and subsequently practised in London before returning to his father’s Christ-Church-lane house. Thomas’s 12 December 1773 marriage to Margaret Duffy at neighbouring St Audoen’s supplies a particular same-name adult, same year and immediate locality, rather than a Scotland-wide name comparison. A young tradesman returning to the family business and marrying later that year is the preferred explanation. The later Christ-Church-lane to 20 Ormond Quay sequence supports continuity of the watchmaking business. The separate marriage and apprenticeship evidence together justify preferring Philip to the unsupported Thomas-173 father attachment.

The 67% rates the complete profile-level father proposition, including identification of the 1773 groom with the advertised watchmaker and of the named Philip with the elder account. Neither the marriage index nor the Duffy pedigree gives Thomas’s trade, address or father’s forename. The advertisement is reused from the 7 October full-page OCR reading; its original image was not newly inspected. The older Philip account contains some junior events, so the elder/junior distinction remains material. Thomas’s circa 1753 birth is an estimate: age twenty would make completed apprenticeship plus several years in London compressed, favouring a somewhat older adult without establishing a replacement birth year. No date is changed. The rare surname, close locality and year are correlated clues, not independent parent statements.

Retain Thomas [[Glasco-173]] as an unselected, previously ungraded father alternative, and retain a distinct unrepresented Thomas watchmaker as an identity alternative. Thomas-173, father with Catherine of Sarah in 1760, is chronologically compatible with the trade cluster, but connecting that household to the 1773 groom adds an unsupported generation, whereas the advertisement names Philip. Thomas-143 could represent the tradesman only if his very weak circa 1766 estimate is revised; the date is not a hard exclusion. The 1779 Miss Hynes marriage and the 1785 Mary King licence may concern remarriages, but no spouse death or identity bridge establishes that sequence. No merge, new wife or new child follows.

The current Catherine Mangan mother attachment and Thomas-143 child attachment remain separately ungraded; Philip’s spouse is not thereby proved to be Thomas’s mother. The selected father replaces one existing local working attachment. Two already-catalogued descendants move into the main working component; the old Thomas-173 account remains separate. No new person, live WikiTree edit or confidence-only upgrade is claimed. The earlier Scottish ancestry assigned to Philip remains uncertain and does not become probable through this change.

Check the original 1773 advertisement and marriage entry, the Duffy 1774/1775 probate papers, and Thomas’s London apprenticeship/freedom records for trade, address or named kin. Seek the 1777 Margaret Glasco grant and the full 1777 Philip/Thomas chancery bill before accepting a Duffy–Hynes remarriage or a precise Philip generation.

Earlier statements that no parent or occupational identity is selected are superseded by this dated, expressly probable working inference. The underlying passages and previous assessments remain below for comparison.


* Thomas’s birth and death dates are unknown.
* His birthplace and residence are not stated.
* His occupation and parentage have not been identified.
* No marriage date or place has yet been found.
* The surname is written as '''Glascoe''' in the pedigree. Searches should also consider variants such as Glasco, Glascow and Glasgow.
* Thomas should not be assigned a Dublin birthplace solely because his father-in-law lived at Back Lane, Dublin.
* Patrick Duffy’s probate record may contain further information about Thomas and Margaret.

A possible identification concerns Glasco, Dublin watch and clock maker. Under Robbery And Reward, the shop of Messrs Peter and Semple at 108 Grafton Street was entered and stolen watches listed. One is a gold double-cased watch marked “Glasco and Son, Dublin.” The stolen watch bears the number 3203.<ref>Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-11, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050127957/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-13, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050128500/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-15, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050129060/ record]; Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1811-03-18, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050129538/ record].</ref> This is a maker/firm mark on a watch listed among stolen property in a robbery notice. The issue dates the printed notice, not manufacture or continuous business activity; “and Son” does not prove named father and son. The watch is not established as made in the existing watchmaker’s shop, and no individual or family identity follows. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Possible Thomas Glascoe of Tinicum Island ===
Thomas reports $115 stolen from his Tinicum Island house on 31 March 1799; the April 9 notice is reprinted on April 11.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/586542475/ Aurora General Advertiser, 1799-04-09, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/586542512/ Aurora General Advertiser, 1799-04-11, p.1].</ref>

Thomas is the subscriber and reported theft victim; William Steel is the alleged thief. The reports do not name Thomas’s family or connect him with the Dublin Glasco households.

This may concern [[Glasco-144]]. Chronologically compatible Thomas Glasco profile; no Tinicum or Delaware identification is established.
